_meta.note: Authored overlay merged by build.py onto the catalog. Regenerate via the workflow; hand-edits are fine.

veganVariant.note: One ingredient swap — the Greek yoghurt finish — makes this fully vegan; everything else is already plant-based.
swaps: replace the 2–3 tbsp Greek yoghurt with plain plant yoghurt (oat or soy gives the closest tang)

veganVariant.note: The mushroom-pak choi-black pepper base is the dish; tofu replaces the egg for protein and a tahini-vinegar drizzle replaces the yolk sauce.
swaps: Replace the 2–3 eggs with 200g firm tofu, pressed and sliced 1cm thick
Fry the tofu in the same hot oiled pan — leave it alone until deeply golden, ~3–4 min per side, before flipping
Mix 1 tbsp tahini with 1 tbsp water and a splash of red wine vinegar; drizzle over the finished dish in place of the broken yolk
veganVariant.steps: hard-brown mushrooms in oil, season hard with black pepper → add garlic and pak choi (stems then leaves) with a splash of water, wilt, hit with vinegar → fry tofu slices until deeply golden both sides → slide over veg, drizzle tahini-vinegar sauce, finish with pepper and vinegar

veganVariant.note: Crumbled firm tofu replaces the eggs, keeping the lift-out-and-fold-back structure; the result is golden and protein-rich rather than glossy-soft.
swaps: Replace the 3 eggs with 200g firm tofu, drained and crumbled into large chunks — cook in hot oil, stirring, until the edges turn golden (~3 min), then lift out and proceed exactly as written
Season the tofu with a pinch of turmeric alongside the salt for colour
veganVariant.steps: crumble + salt + turmeric tofu → cook in hot oil until golden-edged, lift out → char shredded cabbage hard until edges blacken and go sweet → add garlic + chilli → splash vinegar to deglaze, fold the tofu back through, season

veganVariant.note: The egg is a supporting act — firm tofu gives the same chunky protein without boiling.
swaps: Replace the 2–3 eggs with 150 g firm tofu, cubed roughly egg-sized and folded in at the end
veganVariant.steps: quick-pickle sliced onion in vinegar and salt → chop tomato, drain chickpeas, cube firm tofu → fold everything with oil, lemon, chilli, salt and pepper

veganVariant.note: The sauce is already vegan; swap firm tofu for the eggs to keep distinct protein pockets in the pan.
swaps: Replace the 4 eggs with 200g firm tofu, pressed dry and cut into 4 large chunks — nestle into the wells, cover and heat through for 5 minutes
No tofu? Skip the wells and add a second drained tin of chickpeas to the sauce instead
veganVariant.steps: soften onion + pepper in oil → add garlic, cumin, chilli → pour in tomato + chickpeas, simmer to a thick sauce → press in tofu chunks, cover and heat through 5 min → season and serve

veganVariant.note: Crumbled firm tofu takes the egg's place and gives a similar soft texture; nutritional yeast fills in the savoury depth the egg provides.
swaps: replace the 3–4 eggs with 200g firm tofu, drained and crumbled into rough pieces — fold in at step 3 and warm through rather than scramble
add 1 tbsp nutritional yeast off the heat with the lemon
add a pinch of turmeric to the peas for colour
veganVariant.steps: bloom garlic in oil → simmer peas → fold in crumbled tofu to warm through → off heat: nutritional yeast, lemon, chilli, pepper, final drizzle of oil

veganVariant.note: The mushroom-spinach base is already vegan; chickpeas replace the eggs as protein, crisped in the same pan.
swaps: Replace the 2–3 eggs with a drained 400 g tin of chickpeas — add them with the garlic and chilli and crisp at the edges for 2–3 min
Stir in a teaspoon of nutritional yeast with the spinach for the savoury depth the yolk would have given
veganVariant.steps: Sear mushrooms hard until deep golden → add garlic, chilli & chickpeas, crisp 2–3 min → pile in spinach with nutritional yeast to wilt → finish with lemon

veganVariant.note: Avocado replaces the jammy eggs — same fatty richness fanned over the chickpeas, and the dish needs no cooking at all.
swaps: Replace the 2 eggs (and the boiling step) with ½–1 ripe avocado, sliced or roughly broken over the top
veganVariant.steps: fork-smash chickpeas with lemon, oil, chilli, salted onion → dress raw spinach, pile on the chickpeas, fan sliced avocado over the top, finish with oil, lemon, pepper

veganVariant.note: The oats-and-peas base is already vegan; only the egg topping needs swapping.
swaps: Replace the 1–2 eggs with 100g drained tinned chickpeas, crisped in the wiped pan with a splash of oil and an extra pinch of cumin for 3–4 min until golden, then spoon over the oats
veganVariant.steps: temper onion, garlic, cumin & chilli in oil → stir in oats, water & peas, simmer to creamy → crisp chickpeas in the same pan → plate the oats, top with chickpeas, lemon & a pinch more chilli

veganVariant.note: The frizzled egg and its runny yolk are gone; crispy chickpeas in the same hot oil give comparable texture and protein without rebuilding the dish.
swaps: replace the 2 eggs with 6 tbsp drained tinned chickpeas, crisped in the generous hot oil for 3–4 min until they pop and brown, then scatter over the hummus
veganVariant.steps: toast the bread → spread thick with hummus → crisp drained chickpeas in hot oil until they pop and brown, scatter over the hummus → bloom paprika & chilli in the same hot oil and pour over → finish with lemon, salt, pepper

veganVariant.note: Gram flour (chickpea flour) whisked into cold water sets firm under a lid and flips and slices exactly like the egg version — you get a legitimate stovetop farinata with the same wedge-and-keep logic.
swaps: Replace the 6 eggs with 150g gram flour whisked smooth into 300ml cold water, well-seasoned — pour it over the cooked veg exactly as the batter step says
Stir 2 tbsp nutritional yeast into the batter for savoury depth in place of egg flavour
veganVariant.steps: soften onion + pepper, then garlic + spinach → pour seasoned gram-flour batter over, cover, cook low until set firm throughout (~20 min) → flip onto a plate and back into the pan, finish 2–3 min → cool, cut into wedges

veganVariant.note: The spiced tomato-spinach base does the heavy lifting; chickpeas slot in cleanly as the protein.
swaps: replace 1–2 tins of mackerel with 1 tin of chickpeas (drained and rinsed), stirred in with the spinach and simmered for 2 minutes
veganVariant.steps: soften onion in oil → bloom garlic + spices → add tomato, simmer to a thick base → stir in spinach and chickpeas, simmer 2 min → finish with lemon, salt, pepper

veganVariant.note: One swap makes this fully vegan: Greek yoghurt for plain unsweetened soy yoghurt — same off-heat technique, same silky-tangy finish.
swaps: Replace the 3–4 tbsp Greek yoghurt with plain unsweetened soy yoghurt; coconut yoghurt also works for a slightly richer, rounder sauce.

veganVariant.note: Tofu and tomato is a genuine Chinese pairing — you lose the silky curd texture but the dish stays recognizable and satisfying.
swaps: Replace the 3 eggs with 200g firm tofu, pressed dry and torn into rough 2–3 cm chunks; season with a pinch of salt before cooking
Pan-fry the tofu chunks in hot oil until golden on at least one side, then lift out — same point in the recipe as the eggs
veganVariant.steps: press + salt tofu, tear into chunks → fry in hot oil until golden, lift out → soften onion + garlic, cook tomato to a loose sauce → fold tofu back in, season

veganVariant.note: Only the Greek yoghurt needs to change — thick coconut or soy yoghurt gives the same creamy, protein-carrying base.
swaps: Replace the 150–200g Greek yoghurt with the same quantity of thick coconut or soy yoghurt
If using the optional sweetener from 'Level it up', use maple syrup rather than honey
